title: 1968 AHSME Problem 11
statement: If an arc of \(60^\circ\) on circle \(\mathrm{I}\) has the same length as an arc of \(45^\circ\) on circle \(\mathrm{II},\) the ratio of the area of circle \(\mathrm{I}\) to that of circle \(\mathrm{II}\) is:

solutions.text:
Equal arc lengths give \(60r_1=45r_2,\) so \(\frac{r_1}{r_2}=\frac{3}{4}.\) Circle areas scale as the squares of the radii, giving \(A_1:A_2=9:16.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Equate \((\frac{\theta}{360^\circ})2\pi r\) for the two arcs
Square the resulting radius ratio to get the area ratio
